speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a fever and altered mental status; to start our evaluation, how old are you and have you had any recent head trauma or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your age and altered mental status with fever, I need to know if you have any recent travel, insect bites, or tick exposure, and have you noticed any rash or petechiae on your skin?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Comprehensive metabolic panel, Blood cultures, and CT Head.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

The clinical picture of fever, altered mentation, and generalized rigidity in a patient taking haloperidol is classic for NMS, which the previous doctor misidentified as a migraine. I have requested a CBC, metabolic panel, blood cultures, and a CT Head to rule out infection and structural causes; pending those results, NMS remains the primary working diagnosis.
